title: 10 Things I Hate About You
tagline: Paintball, poetry and a proper dessert.
about: A new kid pays the school bad boy to date the sharp-tongued older sister so he can take out the younger one.
cue: Serve the snacks when Patrick starts singing to Kat across the football bleachers.

phone:
Padua High10 Things I Hate About YouPaintball, poetry and a proper dessert.Every recipe serves 4.
    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersBogey's party spinach dipHot baked spinach and artichoke dip with cream cheese and mozzarellaHow to make it250g cream cheese, softened100g sour cream250g frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry1 jar artichoke hearts, drained and chopped1 garlic clove, crushed100g mozzarella, grated1 baguette, sliced and toastedMix the cream cheese, sour cream, spinach, artichokes, garlic and mozzarella and spoon into a baking dish.Bake at 190°C until bubbling. Meanwhile slice and toast the baguette.Serve the dip hot with the toasted baguette.Cameron's croque monsieur squaresHam and gruyere sandwiches under creamy béchamel, grilled and cut smallHow to make it30g butter1 tbsp plain flour250ml milk8 slices of white bread2 tbsp Dijon mustard200g leg ham200g gruyere, gratedMelt the butter, stir in the flour and cook for a minute. Whisk in the milk and simmer until thick to make the bechamel.Spread the bread with Dijon and fill with ham and some of the gruyere.Top with bechamel and the rest of the cheese. Grill until bubbling and golden, then cut into small squares.MainsProm night pastaPenne in a creamy vodka tomato sauce with parmesan and basilHow to make it500g penne3 garlic cloves, crushed1 tsp chilli flakes2 tbsp olive oil400g crushed tomatoes60ml vodka200ml thickened cream100g parmesan, grated1 cup basil leaves, tornSoften the garlic and chilli in the oil. Add the tomatoes and vodka and simmer.Stir in the cream until the sauce turns rosy. Meanwhile cook the penne in salted water until al dente.Toss the pasta through the sauce and finish with parmesan and basil.Seattle salmon burgers with dill mayoPadua High in the rainy Pacific NorthwestHow to make itAs written, serves 4Salmon chopped with spring onion, lemon zest and panko, seared into patties and served in toasted brioche buns with dill mayo, rocket and pickled cucumber.Slice a Lebanese cucumber thinly and soak in 3 tbsp rice vinegar with a pinch of sugar and salt.Chop 600g skinless salmon finely and mix with 2 sliced spring onions, lemon zest, 50g panko, an egg and salt.Shape into 4 patties and chill 20 minutes.Sear in oil for 3 minutes a side.Mix 4 tbsp mayonnaise with chopped dill and lemon juice.Build in toasted brioche buns with rocket and pickles.SweetsTen things browniesFudgy dark chocolate brownies cut in ten squares, each topped differentlyHow to make it200g dark chocolate150g butter250g caster sugar3 eggs100g plain flour125g raspberries50g mixed nuts, choppedflaky salt, to tasteMelt the chocolate and butter together and let it cool slightly. Whisk in the sugar and eggs, then fold in the flour.Pour into a lined tin and bake at 170°C. Cool completely in the tin.Cut into ten squares and top each differently with raspberries, nuts, salt flakes or anything you like.DrinksClub Skunk iced vanilla latteEspresso shaken with vanilla syrup, poured over ice and cold milkHow to make it80g caster sugar80ml water1 vanilla bean, split250ml very strong coffee, or 4 espresso shots600ml cold milk1 bag iceSimmer the sugar, water and vanilla bean for 3 minutes. Cool and remove the bean.Brew the strong coffee and let it cool.Shake the coffee with 2 tablespoons of the syrup and a handful of ice until frothy.Fill four tall glasses with ice and the cold milk, then pour the frothy coffee slowly over the top so it sits in layers.
